text:
sami: Quick question — if we set a feature flag default OFF at the org level, can a lower scope (project/route/model) turn it ON by default? wondering about the exact override rules. :thinking:

lee: Specificity wins. Our rule is: model > route > project > org. More specific scopes override less specific ones.

anya: Follow-up — how do canary audiences interact with that? e.g., org default OFF, but model-level canary 10% ON. If a route tries to set 100% ON, which takes precedence?

kevin: Good question. Policy we agreed on in the last sync: a child scope can only expand a parent's enabled percentage up to a hard cap defined by the parent unless the parent explicitly sets `allow_escalation: true`. So in your example, route cannot go to 100% if the model's canary cap is 10% and the parent disallows escalation.

lee: Example config pattern (YAML):
```yaml
org_defaults:
  feature_x:
    enabled: false
    max_child_pct: 0
    allow_escalation: false

project_a:
  feature_x:
    enabled: false
    max_child_pct: 20
    allow_escalation: false

model_v2:
  feature_x:
    enabled: true
    rollout_pct: 10
    allow_escalation: false

route:/generate-text:
  feature_x:
    enabled: true
    rollout_pct: 100  # will be capped to 10 because model_v2 sets rollout_pct=10 and allows no escalation
```

kevin: Implementation note: the evaluation order is: collect effective parent limits walking up scopes, compute min(max_child_pct, parent_rollout_pct, ancestor_caps), then apply the local intent. This prevents accidental full rollouts under a nested canary.

rollout-bot: :robot_face: Canary created: model_v2/feature_x -> 10% (created by kevin at 1891234575)

sami: Thanks — can we also enforce a lint/CI check that rejects PRs which try to set `rollout_pct` > ancestor cap unless `allow_escalation: true` exists in the ancestor? I'll open a small PR with the rule. @kevin can you review when I ping it?

kevin: Yup — will review. Also recommend adding an audit warning in the console when a route-level toggle is blocked by a parent cap (so product sees why it didn't turn on). :+1:

sami: Awesome, thanks all. Keeping this thread as the design note for enforcement behaviour.
